title: SliceBound fairness-aware canary with retention replay
author: Asha Menon
release_notes: Introduces SliceBound canary orchestrator for fairness-aware rollouts with retention-enabled shadow capture and bounded rollback policies. Requires console opt-in and a migration step for experiment metadata.
description: Context and motivation: Many customers operating under fairness/regulatory constraints asked for canary tooling that ensures rollout decisions consider slice-level fairness metrics (parity, calibration drift) in addition to standard SLOs. This PR introduces a new orchestrator mode — 'SliceBound' — which: 1) computes per-slice metrics during shadow and canary phases; 2) enforces minimum-exposure constraints so small cohorts aren't overrepresented; 3) stores redacted shadow traces (retention replay) for post-mortem and audit replay; and 4) implements a bounded rollback policy that limits disruptive rollbacks by staging decreases in traffic via rate-limited backoff. Design summary: The SliceBound controller hooks into the rollout evaluation pipeline and takes a configured list of slices (by attribute selectors). During shadow seeding an online aggregator computes slice-level delta signals (latency, token-loss, fairness parity). A decision rule engine evaluates multi-objective constraints (SLOs + fairness tolerances) and emits one of: hold, continue, bounded-decrement, abort-and-revert. Retention replay: shadowed requests are captured with a privacy-first pipeline: PII fields are tokenized, sensitive context is hashed, and replay artifacts are stored in an encrypted bucket for configurable TTL (default 30 days). These artifacts are surfaced to the replay CLI for deterministic replays against later model snapshots to verify regressions. Safety features: - Minimum-cohort-exposure: no slice receives >X% exposure until it passes smoke gating. - Fairness gates: parity and calibration checks with tunable thresholds; failing any gate triggers bounded-decrement or abort depending on severity. - Cost-aware rollback bounding: rollback decisions consider cost-slo impact and apply ramped traffic decreases (e.g., -10% every 5 minutes) with the option to expedite for severe regressions. Implementation details: - Runtime: controller change (pkg/rollout/slicebound.go) adds evaluation scheduling and slice aggregation. - Storage: replay capture pipeline (services/replay/producer.go) plus a TTL-enforced retention manager (services/replay/retention.go). - Networking: new telemetry tag 'slicebound.slice' added to spans and metrics. - Console: feature flag and per-rollout UI panel with slice heatmaps and replay links (ui/rollouts/SliceBoundPanel.tsx). - Backwards compatibility: existing rollout schemas remain unchanged; SliceBound is opt-in via rollout-spec field 'mode: "slicebound"'. CI and release notes: "CI: full integration suite ran; a flaky smoke test SIG-AGG-001 was retried and passed. We added a new CI lane 'slicebound-e2e' that exercises replay capture and TTL pruning. Release: opt-in feature behind 'slicebound_rollouts' feature flag; docs updated with migration steps and audit checklist. Operational notes: - Ops must ensure KMS keys for replay buckets are provisioned before enabling; migration job must annotate existing rollout objects with empty slice lists to avoid misclassification. - TTL default is 30 days but must be reduced for regulated tenants; retention manager supports tenant-level overrides. Backwards compatibility and rollback: The rollout API remains backward compatible. The controller includes an emergency-evacuate endpoint to immediately stop shadow captures for a tenant. Merge outcome: squash-merged into main after reviewers approved and successful CI. Follow-ups: add a demo notebook for replay-driven debugging (ENG-321), and a periodic job to auto-expire old replay artifacts in air-gapped installs (PM-48).
